meta.title: Timeline view
meta.description: Timeline view in React Scheduler: how it behaves by default, what you can configure, its accessibility, and its limits.

demos.columns: How many columns an hour may use
demos.columnPlacement: Which item takes the left column
demos.overflowWindow: How far a "+ more" group may reach

basics.intro: The timeline draws the rendered shifts as one continuous grid, from the first shift's start to the last one's end. Items are placed at the minute they start and are as tall as they last, so a glance shows how a day is filled rather than only what is in it. Set view="timeline", or let the reader switch views with defaultView.
basics.grid: The grid is hourHeight pixels per elapsed hour, with one label per hour and a boundary line at every shift change inside the range. Hours outside the shift being read are drawn as off-shift bands, so a night that runs past midnight stays one grid instead of two days.
parts: An item without an end is given defaultDuration, and one shorter than minCardHeight is drawn at that height so its title stays readable.
Items that overlap share the lane in columns, up to maxColumns of them.
What does not fit the columns is collected into a group reached through a + more chip, which opens the overflow dialog.

accessibility.intro: The timeline is a list of items with a position, not a picture of one. Everything the grid says visually is also said in text.
points: Each card is a button: it is in the tab order, and <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> opens its detail.
A card's accessible name carries its level and its time, so the position in the grid never has to be read to know what an item is.
Shift headers are real headings, and their level follows headingLevel, so the page keeps one outline.
The now marker and the boundary lines are decorative; the time they mark is in the hour labels and in each card's name.
Color is never the only carrier: the level a color stands for is also written on the card.

customization.intro: Everything below is a field of timeline. The defaults are what the demos above show; the demos here change one field at a time.
customization.placement: columnPlacement decides which column an item takes when several overlap. 'priority', the default, groups the items that overlap, orders them with compareItems, and may promote an item out of the overflow group into a column that frees up. 'time' keeps plain start order and skips that promotion, so an item that started earlier keeps its column.
customization.overflow: overflowMergeWindow bounds how much time one + more group may cover. Consecutive hours merge into one group only while the merged group stays inside the window, so a busy morning becomes several honest groups rather than one that spans the shift.
customization.options: The full list, generated from the package's declarations:

points: The grid covers the rendered shifts only. Reading further back or forward is navigation between shifts, not scrolling past the end of the grid.
Items are placed by timestamp in the reader's own time zone; the package does not take a time zone of its own yet (see the roadmap).
Cards that overlap share the lane in equal columns. A column cannot be made wider than its neighbours.
The timeline does not virtualize its rows: a range of a few days at the default hourHeight is a tall document.
Items cannot be moved or resized here. Editing is planned, not shipped.
